meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen's essay, and the zero you gave him.
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. So what do you actually have?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. A paste from another file looks exactly like that. Did anyone ask Owen where his drafts were before that zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
You didn't answer me. Was Owen heard before that zero, yes or no? Whatever this turns out to be, it stays off his record and it stays between us.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Act 3, Scene 2 isn't the whole play, Hale. Is that line anywhere in Hamlet, in any edition?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
I'll be checking that myself tonight. So what are you proposing?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument after an outline; that's what outlines are for. And you still haven't answered me about what you're proposing.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's your own procedure, and I'll hold you to every word of it in writing tonight. Owen does the rewrite to put this behind him, and I want the date before I leave this room. That isn't him admitting anything.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth, after school. I'll confirm it with Owen and answer your email tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, after school on Thursday, November 12, not in front of his class, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still want a plain answer to whether Owen was heard before that zero was entered, and every term above confirmed in writing. I expect that in writing from you tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record; she still wants those terms confirmed in writing tonight and a straight answer on whether Owen was heard first. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it well before her call.
What moved her: You turned the screen and showed the version history with its exact times, because it was dated, tied to Owen's own document, and something she could check on the spot.
What cost ground: You never answered whether Owen was spoken to before the zero went in, and with a procedure-minded litigator an unanswered process question stays open and ends up in the email to the principal.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on the night before it was due, which came very close to that kind of late October night. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether Owen was heard before the zero, answer it directly with a yes or no and what you did under procedure 4.1, before showing the next piece of evidence.
